kept.q: What is the composition of an alpha particle released during the radioactive decay of a heavy nuclide?
options: 2 protons and 2 neutrons, with no electrons
kept.explanation: An alpha particle is identical to a helium nucleus, made up of 2 protons and 2 neutrons bound together with no electrons. This gives it a mass number of 4 and a charge of +2.
kept.pidgin: Alpha particle be like helium nucleus, e get 2 protons and 2 neutrons, no electron dey inside. Na why e get mass number 4 and charge +2.

kept.q: A hospital in Kano stores 80 g of Phosphorus-32, which has a half-life of 14 days, for use in cancer treatment. How many grams of the isotope will remain after 42 days?
kept.explanation: 42 days divided by the 14-day half-life gives 3 half-lives. Starting with 80 g: after 1 half-life = 40 g, after 2 = 20 g, after 3 = 10 g remaining.
kept.pidgin: 42 days divide by 14 days half-life give 3 half-lives. 80g reduce to 40g, then 20g, then 10g after the 3rd half-life.

kept.q: Sodium-22 (atomic number 11) undergoes positron emission to form Neon-22 (atomic number 10). In the nuclear equation Na-22 -> Ne-22 + X, what is particle X?
options: A positron, with mass number 0 and charge +1
A beta particle, with mass number 0 and charge -1
A neutron, with mass number 1 and charge 0
A proton, with mass number 1 and charge +1
kept.explanation: The mass number stays the same (22 to 22) but the atomic number drops by 1 (11 to 10), which matches emission of a positron (mass number 0, charge +1). This balances both mass and charge in the equation.
kept.pidgin: Mass number no change (22 to 22) but atomic number drop by 1 (11 to 10). Na positron get mass number 0 and charge +1, e dey balance the equation well well.

kept.q: In a natural radioactive decay series, Uranium-238 (atomic number 92, mass number 238) decays through several alpha and beta emissions to finally form a stable isotope of Lead-206 (atomic number 82, mass number 206). Calculate the total number of alpha particles emitted in this series.
kept.explanation: Only alpha emission changes the mass number (by 4 each time); beta emission does not affect mass number. The total mass number drop is 238 - 206 = 32, so the number of alpha particles is 32 divided by 4, which equals 8.
